vectors.title: A sale within the year is short-term; FIFO takes the earliest lot first
Publication 544: bought 2024-06-17; sold 2025-06-17 is short-term, 2025-06-18 long-term
Publication 550: bought 2024-01-31; sold 2025-01-29 short-term, sold 2025-02-06 long-term
Acquired 29 February: its anniversary is 28 February, so 1 March is the first long-term day
365 elapsed days across 29 February are not more than one year (RP2's US plugin says long-term)
Dates are UTC dates: an evening purchase in New York is the next day's lot (a documented choice)
LIFO (a standing specific identification) takes the latest lot first
HIFO takes the highest unit cost first, ties by acquisition
LOFO takes the lowest unit cost first
Per wallet: a lot moved away is not the source wallet's any more (RP2's per-wallet engine sells it twice)
A move's fee units leave with their basis and realize nothing; the moved units keep their acquisition date and basis
Global (universal) scope before 2025: the earliest lot of any wallet goes first
Global scope with a 2025 disposal fails closed: § 1.1012-1(j) identifies per wallet from 2025

refusal.reason: Treas. Reg. § 1.1012-1(j): from 2025 basis is identified per wallet or account

vectors.title: Staking rewards are ordinary income at fair market value on receipt, which is also their basis (Rev. Rul. 2023-14)
Mining, interest and airdrops are ordinary income by kind (Notice 2014-21, Rev. Rul. 2019-24)
A sale's network fee units are disposed of with it at the sale's USD amount
Paying for goods or services with bitcoin disposes of it at the value received
Form 8949 boxes: C/F before 2025, I/L for 2025 and 2026; no table yet for 2027 (unknown)
Rev. Proc. 2024-28 example facts per wallet: each wallet sells its own units
Per wallet, a sale larger than the wallet's units fails closed even when other wallets hold enough
A lot that moves away and back is one portion again; FIFO keeps acquisition order
At one instant, acquisitions, then moves, then disposals: a move funds a same-instant sale at its destination
